keynote.name: Peter Nilsson
keynote.bookTitle: Irreplaceable: How AI Changes Everything (And Nothing) in Teaching and Learning
keynote.bio: Educator, author and musician with over 20 years in schools as head of school, administrator, teacher, tutor, coach and board member. Most recently Head of School at King’s Academy in Jordan; before that he taught English and digital humanities at Deerfield Academy. Founder of Athena Lab and editor of The Educator’s Notebook; he has spoken at the OECD, the College Board and NAIS, and serves on the advisory boards of SXSW EDU and the Center for Curriculum Redesign.

workshops.title: When the Machine Can Do the Maths: What’s Left to Teach When AI Solves the Problem?
workshops.description: AI can now solve almost every problem in our curriculum in seconds — which forces an uncomfortable question for every subject, not just maths: if the machine can produce the answer, what are we actually here to teach? This session reframes mathematics from answer-getting (now largely automatable) toward the durable skills AI can’t replace: reasoning, justification, modelling real situations, and recognising when a confident output is simply wrong. Working from concrete before-and-after examples, participants will see how familiar tasks and assessments can be redesigned to stay meaningful in an AI-saturated classroom — protecting academic integrity without resorting to bans. The framework is deliberately transferable: every head of department leaves with a lens to apply to their own subject.
workshops.learn: Distinguish answer-getting from the reasoning, justification and modelling skills that remain valuable; apply a simple framework for redesigning tasks and assessments; protect academic integrity without bans or detection tools; redesign one of your own tasks during the session.

workshops.title: Emotional Intelligence: In this new age of AI, how do we as educators help our students (and ourselves) grow in EQ
workshops.description: For students to thrive in a global world, they will not only need a strong IQ but also a high EQ. Communication, understanding and empathising with the opinions and feelings of others, and knowing how to make decisions are all involved in this area. Participants will learn about emotional intelligence for their own lives, and how to practically help their students grow in this key area.
workshops.learn: The main points of emotional intelligence; how to grow in EQ yourself; how to help students grow in EQ.

workshops.title: Rethinking Assessment in the Classroom
workshops.role: Head of Language Acquisition, Middle / High School
workshops.description: Effective assessment is more than assigning grades — it is a powerful tool for supporting and improving student learning. Participants will explore the key characteristics of high-quality assessment and, through practical examples and collaborative activities, examine how to design meaningful assessment tasks, develop clear success criteria and rubrics, and make assessment more transparent and objective for students.
workshops.learn: Apply the key characteristics of high-quality assessment; check your own assessments against them; analyse good and bad examples; explore how students can take responsibility for their own learning.

workshops.title: Teaching Critical Thinking to Support Student Learning & Growth
workshops.description: A practical session exploring simple, effective strategies teachers can use tomorrow to develop pupils’ critical thinking: questioning techniques, discussion strategies, and classroom activities that encourage pupils to think deeply, make connections, explain their reasoning, and become more independent learners. Practical and interactive, with a focus on discussion and group work.
workshops.learn: Practical strategies for using discussion and group work to develop pupils’ critical thinking, collaboration and communication.

workshops.title: Designing Choice: Rethinking Engagement Through Culture
workshops.role: High School Academic Director, DP Coordinator
workshops.description: An interactive session on the relationship between choice, engagement and culture in the classroom. While 21st-century approaches emphasise learner autonomy and inquiry, could the choices we provide sometimes create hidden constraints? Through the lens of culturally responsive teaching, participants examine how students from different backgrounds may experience motivation, engagement and agency differently, and how classroom practices can be adapted thoughtfully rather than applied universally.
workshops.learn: How choice, engagement, motivation and agency connect; how cultural and educational backgrounds shape students’ comfort with autonomy, inquiry, participation and decision-making.

workshops.title: Start at 13, Not 16: Why University Readiness Belongs in Middle School
workshops.description: By the time most students begin university counselling, critical windows for building direction, skills and confidence have already closed. This session presents a field-tested alternative: a two-semester Uni Prep curriculum for Grade 8, built and delivered at Muras International School, Osh — career exploration, goal-setting, 21st-century skills, study habits and the basics of global higher education, with a no-grades, reflection-based assessment model.
workshops.learn: A tested framework for starting university readiness in middle school, with tools for early career exploration and goal-setting; a worksheet to map your own school’s readiness timeline.

workshops.title: Going Forward by Looking Back
workshops.description: In our push for technology, we have forgotten to teach our children about life outside the screens. Children are no longer connected to the natural world or the tactility of the human body. This session introduces teachers to outdoor learning and the value of old-school survival skills. No screens allowed!
workshops.learn: The outdoors is the cheapest and best teaching resource you will ever need.

workshops.title: ‘Flipped’ vs Traditional Pedagogy: Case Study in Mathematical Physics
workshops.role: AP Calculus and AP Physics Teacher
workshops.description: Compares key aspects of flipped versus traditional teaching, first tried in a university Statics course at the University at Buffalo (SUNY) and later in high-school maths and physics. Student performance improved measurably and academic integrity improved with it — but the shift needs additional instructional staff. Student survey opinions argue for a consistent semester-long approach and flexibility for different learning styles.
workshops.learn: A data-informed rationale for flipped-classroom pedagogy; ideas to try in your own classroom.

workshops.title: Making Learning Meaningful: Interactive Teaching with Simple Resources
workshops.description: How teachers can create engaging, meaningful learning experiences with simple, low-cost resources — hands-on, playful, and connected to children’s real-life experiences. Adaptable examples across subjects in Early Years and Primary; in the last part, participants use everyday materials to design their own short interactive learning activity.
workshops.learn: One or two new ideas to use in your lessons, and an understanding of meaningful learning.

workshops.title: Conquering the Class Clown: Answering your Classroom Management Questions
workshops.description: Tips, tricks, and collaborative discussions on how to maintain positive human connections in the classroom.
workshops.learn: Practical ideas for kindly redirecting student behaviour and creating an atmosphere where positive collaboration is possible.

workshops.title: Differentiated English Teaching: Reproductive, Productive, and Creative Tasks with AI Support
workshops.role: English Teacher, Teach for Kyrgyzstan alumna
workshops.description: Every English classroom includes students at different levels of readiness, yet tasks are often designed for one average level. A model of differentiated instruction built on three task types — reproductive, productive and creative — with how AI tools can quickly generate differentiated tasks at each level, and how assessment and feedback fit the model. Drawn from Grade 6 teaching and master’s research.
workshops.learn: A three-level framework for differentiating tasks that works in any subject; using AI to generate differentiated tasks quickly; assessing progress meaningfully across levels.

workshops.title: Social-Emotional Learning in Primary School
workshops.description: What Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) means and why it matters; how to include SEL in everyday classroom activities and routines; and how SEL practices help students manage emotions, build positive relationships, communicate and make responsible decisions — and how SEL affects engagement, behaviour, confidence and learning.
workshops.learn: Different SEL practices and simple ways to use them to create a positive, supportive and welcoming classroom.

workshops.title: Rapid Game Design for Your Classroom
workshops.description: A game does things a worksheet cannot: a student can take a real risk and see what happens without it costing anything that matters, and the shared story it produces is unusually good ground for reflection. The obstacle has always been design time — and AI is now a capable design partner that argues about rules, proposes alternatives and plays out every sequence of your dice. We walk the full pipeline on a topic the room chooses, with a worked IGCSE Business example. The game itself ends up on paper — no screens when it is played.
workshops.learn: How to get from a curriculum objective to a playable game. Leave with a checklist, an example, and the start of your own game.

workshops.title: Beyond the Answer: Making Primary Mathematics Real, Reasoned and Relevant
workshops.description: Mathematics should not stop at finding the correct answer. This session shows how to contextualise primary mathematics through real-world situations and put the emphasis on the “why” behind mathematical thinking — what information matters, which strategy fits, whether the answer makes sense — with language as a key part of understanding and communicating reasoning.
workshops.learn: Practical ways to connect maths to real life, use language to build understanding of context, and use story-based tasks to develop problem-solving and communication.

workshops.title: Inquiry in Action: Engaging Every Learner
workshops.role: Head of Language Acquisition in PYP
workshops.description: How inquiry-based learning supports engagement, meaningful communication and deeper thinking. Starting with a provocation, participants move through interactive stations on the inquiry cycle, inquiry phases and language support — with a focus on open-ended questions, the teacher as facilitator, and scaffolding so every learner can take part.
workshops.learn: The stages of the inquiry cycle; an inquiry-based lesson experienced as a learner; jigsaw reading as a research strategy; analysing and connecting information.

workshops.title: Collaboration & Communication Among Students
workshops.description: Ways to group students, provide feedback, develop self-reflection, and strengthen collaboration among students.
workshops.learn: Helping groups be more effective; evaluating work done in groups; helping students reflect on their contribution and identify areas to grow.

workshops.title: Social-Emotional Learning and Human-Centred Skills
workshops.description: An introduction to Social-Emotional Learning through the five CASEL competencies, built around one question: how might we transform schools from systems of discipline into communities of care? Empathy and human-centred design for learning, with an inclusive welcome, active engagement and a reflective close.
workshops.learn: Analyse the five CASEL competencies; strategies for a human-centred learning environment; a plan to integrate SEL in teaching and learning.

workshops.title: Beyond the Chatbot: Designing Collaborative Classrooms for the AI Era
workshops.description: As AI tools become ubiquitous, students’ ability to collaborate, communicate and build on each other’s ideas matters more than ever. A hands-on design challenge that needs both human ingenuity and critical use of AI, and a practical 4-step framework — Collaboration 4.0 — for designing collaborative projects that build active listening, constructive feedback and shared problem-solving.
workshops.learn: The Collaboration 4.0 framework; five low-prep strategies for collaboration skills; a lesson plan redesigned in a design sprint; positioning AI as a team member rather than a shortcut.

organisers.name: Central Asia Federation of Athletics, Activities and Arts (CAFA)
organisers.text: A regional network connecting international and private schools across Central Asia, including Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan. It brings students and educators together for sport, the arts and academic competition, fostering cooperation, leadership, resilience and sportsmanship.
